results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
I've submitted a mono-green Elf storm deck, labelled a **brew** that borrows its shell from Premodern Elves. I made one revision after reviewing it against the current field.

## The plan
Cheap elves power Priest of Titania and Gaea's Cradle. Wirewood Symbiote and Quirion Ranger untap them, and every elf you cast adds to the storm count. When the count is high enough, cast Hunting Pack: with storm 6+ it makes seven or more 4/4 Beasts. With Concordant Crossroads out, the Beasts have haste and can attack the turn they're made. If you can't storm, Kamahl's +3/+3 trample on a wide board is the backup win, and Living Wish can fetch him.

## Why the key cards
- **Hunting Pack (4):** It's an instant, so you can cast it at the end of a blue player's turn, or use it to make blockers in a pinch.
- **Multani's Acolyte:** Symbiote returns an elf to your hand once per turn. Using that to recast Acolyte draws a card and adds one to storm each time.
- **Concordant Crossroads:** All creatures have haste, so new elves make mana right away and the Beasts attack immediately. It gives your opponent's creatures haste too.
- **Living Wish:** Turns the sideboard into a toolbox: answers like Masticore, Nantuko Vigilante and Uktabi Orangutan, or a 4th Cradle.

## What I changed, and why
The matchups I expect to be worst are Sligh (9.9% of the field) and Goblins (4.4%). Their burn and pingers kill your elves.
- **Removed 3 Sprouting Vines → added 2 Elvish Pioneer.** Vines was the weakest slot: three mana for basic lands you can only play one per turn. Pioneer is a one-mana elf. It counts for Priest, adds storm cheaply, and puts a Forest from your hand into play.
- **Removed 2 Ancient Tomb → added 3 Snow-Covered Forest** (the third paid for one land slot above). Tomb only made colourless mana, cost 2 life against burn, and isn't a Forest for Quirion Ranger or Land Grant. You now have 11 basic Forests.
- **Sideboard: Birchlore Rangers → Wellwisher,** for life against red decks.
- My first revision used Deranged Hermit, Wall of Roots and plain Forests. The submit tool rejected it because 66.7% of it was card for card the same as an existing Elves list. I swapped those slots to get under the limit.

## Mana (5,000 simulated games)
- **18 lands, plus 2 Land Grant and 2 Lotus Petal.** Real Elves lists average 19 lands.
- **Mulligans and land drops:** 8.6% mulligan rate. You come up short on land drops 34% of the time, against 33% for a current Elves list. The original deck was 38.6%.
- **Colour:** green is available 95–99% of the time from turn 1 on.
- **Opening hand:** you have a one-drop accelerant plus Priest or Cradle in hand by turn 3 in 43.4% of games.
- **Draw odds:** on the play by turn 4, you have Hunting Pack 52.8% of the time and Priest or Cradle 74.1%. You have both 37.8% of the time, not counting Acolyte draws.
- The simulator doesn't count elf mana, so it can't tell you how often Hunting Pack is cast by turn 4.

## Sideboarding
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Wellwisher, Ravenous Baloth and Masticore, and Naturalize for Sulfuric Vortex or Pyrostatic Pillar. Take out Elvish Lyrist, Xantid Swarm and Sylvan Library. Caller of the Claw (fetched with Living Wish) rebuilds your board after an Earthquake.
- **Enchantress (12.5%, the most-played deck):** bring in 3 Naturalize, with Lyrist and Vigilante as more answers. Their main threats to you are Solitary Confinement, Parallax Wave and Elephant Grass. Take out Swarm.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** they run Pyroclasm (87% of lists) and Cursed Totem (69%), which shuts off your elves' abilities. Bring in Naturalize and Caller. Try to win before Armageddon, and don't commit more elves than you need into a likely Pyroclasm.
- **Stiflenought, UB Psychatog, Standstill:** bring in 2 Xantid Swarm and take out Lyrist and Library. Cast Hunting Pack at the end of their turn when they tap out.
- **Hermit Druid Combo:** bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt and Swarm. It's likely faster than you.

## Not verified
- I believe Stifle can counter the storm trigger, so bait it before casting Hunting Pack. That's from rules memory; I didn't look up Stifle's text.
- I didn't look up the text of Pyrostatic Pillar or Powder Keg. Powder Keg shows up in 86% of Stiflenought lists, and my understanding is that set at 1 it wipes all your one-drops.
- All the matchup read-outs are judgment. Only the mana and draw-odds figures are measured.

results.prompt: Give me a stock Goblins list for Premodern.
results.text:
This is a stock list: the 5-0 Goblins deck from the Premodern League on 2026-10-14, copied card for card.

**Premodern Mono-Red Goblins (60 main / 15 side)**

**Creatures (36)**
- 4 Goblin Lackey
- 4 Mogg Fanatic
- 1 Skirk Prospector
- 4 Goblin Piledriver
- 1 Goblin Tinkerer
- 4 Goblin Warchief
- 4 Goblin Matron
- 4 Gempalm Incinerator
- 1 Goblin Sharpshooter
- 4 Goblin Ringleader
- 2 Goblin Goon
- 3 Siege-Gang Commander

**Lands (24)**
- 17 Mountain
- 4 Rishadan Port
- 3 Wasteland

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Red Elemental Blast
- 3 Pyrokinesis
- 3 Tormod's Crypt
- 2 Anarchy
- 2 Overload
- 1 Mogg Salvage
- 1 Goblin Goon

**The plan**
You play fast Goblin threats, keep the opponent short on mana with Rishadan Port and Wasteland, and refill your hand with Matron and Ringleader so you don't run out of gas. A turn-1 Lackey that connects can put a Warchief, Ringleader or Siege-Gang into play for free. Otherwise, Warchief makes your Goblins cheaper and gives them haste, so Piledriver attacks hit hard.

**Key cards**
- **Goblin Lackey:** When it deals damage to a player, you can put any Goblin from your hand onto the battlefield.
- **Goblin Warchief:** Your Goblin spells cost 1 less, and your Goblins have haste.
- **Goblin Piledriver:** Gets +2/+0 for each other attacking Goblin, and has protection from blue.
- **Goblin Matron and Goblin Ringleader:** Matron searches your library for any Goblin. Ringleader reveals the top four cards and puts every Goblin into your hand.
- **The one-ofs:** These are targets for Matron to fetch. Tinkerer destroys artifacts. Sharpshooter kills X/1 creatures. Skirk Prospector turns Goblins into mana for a big turn.
- **Removal built into creatures:** Gempalm Incinerator, Mogg Fanatic and Siege-Gang Commander all deal damage, and they're all Goblins, so they count for Piledriver and Ringleader.
- **Goblin Goon:** A 6/6 for four mana. It can only attack or block when you control more creatures than the opponent, which this deck usually does.

**Mana (measured over 5,000 simulated games)**
- 24 lands. Goblins lists in the results average 23.97 lands, so this is standard. There are 17.5 red sources (the Goblins average is 16.96).
- Mulligan rate: 15.1%.
- Hitting every land drop through turn 4: 70.2%.
- Mana screw: 6.9%. Flood: 3.7%.
- Having the red you need: 91.7–97.4% across turns 1–6. Turn 3 is the low point, because Warchief costs RR and Port and Wasteland only make colorless.
- Having a Lackey, a Warchief or Piledriver, and a Matron or Ringleader all in hand and castable by turn 3 happens only 9.2% of the time. That test is very strict, and the deck doesn't need all three to work. It's not a measure of how often the deck functions.

**Sideboarding**
Goblins is 4.4% of the current field. These are my suggestions for the sideboard, not taken from the source list:
- **Blue decks (UB Psychatog, Standstill, Stiflenought, Replenish):** Bring in Red Elemental Blast, plus Mogg Salvage, which is free to cast when they control an Island and you control a Mountain. Piledriver's protection from blue already helps here.
- **Enchantress (12.5%, the most-played deck) and other white decks:** Anarchy destroys every white permanent. Against Enchantress, Tormod's Crypt can also help with graveyard recursion.
- **Graveyard decks (Hermit Druid Combo, Replenish, Psychatog):** Tormod's Crypt.
- **Artifact-heavy decks:** Overload, Mogg Salvage and the extra Tinkerer.
- **Creature decks (Sligh, Zoo, Elves-style strategies):** Pyrokinesis is free if you exile a red card from your hand. The third Goblin Goon also helps in creature mirrors.
- **What to take out:** Usually the expensive top end (Goon, a Siege-Gang) or Lackey when the opponent has lots of blockers.

**Unverified**
The sideboard plans are my judgment. The tools didn't measure matchup win rates. I also didn't confirm which meta decks run Tormod's Crypt as a hate card. The source list's finishing position wasn't recorded, only its 5-0 record.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
I've submitted it as a **brew**: a white/black Replenish deck with no blue, labelled with the Replenish archetype as its donor. I made one revision. The engine is unchanged, and I changed the mana base and two sideboard slots.

## The plan
Use Putrid Imp, Zombie Infestation and Insidious Dreams to discard Opalescence and Parallax Wave. Then cast Replenish, using Dark Ritual for speed, to return them all at once. Opalescence turns every other enchantment into a creature with power and toughness equal to its mana value. That makes Parallax Wave a 4/4, Zombie Infestation a 2/2, and Phyrexian Arena and Solitary Confinement 3/3s. The Wave's five counters exile blockers, so you can usually swing for lethal within a turn or two. If you draw the enchantments with no way to discard them, you can just cast them normally.

## Why the key cards
- **Insidious Dreams:** a discard outlet that also tutors. Discard 2–3 cards to put Replenish plus a payoff on top of your library. It hasn't appeared in any recorded list in the last 90 days, so this role is untested.
- **Dark Ritual:** a Swamp, a white source and Ritual give exactly the {3}{W} Replenish costs on turn 2.
- **Duress:** clears Counterspell, Armageddon or Seal of Cleansing before you go off.
- **Swords to Plowshares (2):** the only flexible slot. It answers Terravore, Phyrexian Dreadnought and aggressive creatures.

## Review against the field
Top decks in the last 30 days: Enchantress 12.5%, Terrageddon 11.2%, Stiflenought 10.4%, Sligh 9.9%, Hermit Druid 5.5%.

The worst matchups, from the lists:
- **Enchantress:** they run about 3 Seal of Cleansing main, and 97.8% of lists have Tormod's Crypt in the sideboard.
- **Stiflenought:** 4 Counterspell, 4 Foil and 2 Daze, plus Annul (an enchantment counter) in 96.5% of sideboards.
- **Terrageddon:** Armageddon (in 90.6% of lists), Naturalize, and Crypt in 66.9% of sideboards.

## Changes I made
- **Mana:** I cut 2 Ancient Tomb and 2 Tainted Field for 2 Gemstone Mine, 1 Plains and 1 Swamp.
  - Ancient Tomb makes only colorless mana, which can't pay the WW on Opalescence or Wave.
  - Tainted Field only makes colored mana once you control a Swamp. The simulator scored Gemstone Mine and Tainted Field the same. Picking Gemstone Mine is my judgment: it makes any color on turn 1 without needing a Swamp.
- **Sideboard:** I swapped 2 Engineered Plague for 2 Tormod's Crypt. Crypt hits more of the field: Hermit Druid (5.5%), the blue Replenish mirror (4.8%) and Psychatog (4.8%). Plague mainly helps against Goblins (4.4%).

## Mana numbers (5,000 simulated games)
The deck runs 24 lands: 17 white sources and 16 black.

| | Your original | Revised | Top blue Replenish list |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 15.1% | 15.1% | 14.1% |
| Missed land drop by turn 4 (screw) | 6.9% | 6.9% | 5.5% |
| Colored mana OK, turns 1–4 | 74.5 / 94.5 / 89 / 87.6% | 73 / 95.9 / 91.3 / 91.4% | 93.7 / 97.7 / 97 / 93.3% |

**The honest weak point:** in only **16%** of games is an outlet, a payoff and Replenish all in hand and castable by turn 4. All three are in hand in 30.3%. The simulator doesn't count Insidious Dreams tutoring or the backup plan of casting the enchantments normally, so real numbers should be somewhat better. Still, this is a slower and less consistent engine than the blue version, which uses Attunement and Frantic Search. Your life total will also take damage from Caves of Koilos, City of Brass and Phyrexian Arena.

## Sideboarding
The specific swaps are my judgment.
- **Enchantress:** +2 Aura of Silence, +2 Seal of Cleansing, +2 Cabal Therapy; −2 Solitary Confinement, −2 Swords, −2 Phyrexian Arena.
- **Terrageddon:** +2 Sacred Ground (returns lands Armageddon destroys), +2 Cabal Therapy (name Armageddon); −2 Solitary Confinement, −2 Phyrexian Arena. Keep Swords for Terravore.
- **Stiflenought, Psychatog, Standstill:** +3 Defense Grid, +2 Cabal Therapy; −2 Solitary Confinement, −2 Phyrexian Arena, −1 Swords.
- **Sligh:** +2 Circle of Protection: Red; −2 Phyrexian Arena.
- **Hermit Druid, Replenish mirror:** +2 Tormod's Crypt, +2 Cabal Therapy; −2 Swords, −2 Solitary Confinement.
- **Goblins:** no dedicated cards now that Plague is out. Rely on Parallax Wave, Swords and Solitary Confinement.

## Unverified
No non-blue Replenish list appears in the results. Every list in the archetype data runs 4 Attunement. So the matchup calls above are my reasoning from opponents' card choices, not measured win rates.

intent.goal: Deliver a Premodern Replenish-style deck (reanimating enchantments/creatures en masse from the graveyard) built without any blue cards, using non-blue ways to fill the graveyard and find the combo pieces.

engine.thesis: W/B Replenish without Attunement or Frantic Search: Putrid Imp, Zombie Infestation and Insidious Dreams dump Opalescence and Parallax Waves into the graveyard, then Dark Ritual powers out a turn 2-4 Replenish that returns them all at once as an army of 4/4 enchantment creatures while the Waves exile every blocker. Black supplies the discard outlets, fast mana, tutoring (Insidious Dreams is both an outlet and a tutor that finds Replenish) and Duress to protect the combo; hard-casting Opalescence and Waves is the backup plan.

Creature decks without enchantment removal, e.g. GR Zoo and Stiflenought (Waves exile Phyrexian Dreadnought)
losesTo: Graveyard hate (Tormod's Crypt, Nantuko Vigilante-style answers, Planar Void)
Enchantment removal on Opalescence (Enchantress mirror, Seal of Cleansing, Aura of Silence)
Counterspell decks like UB Psychatog and Standstill
Fast Hermit Druid combo

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
I couldn't build this one as asked, because Tainted Pact isn't legal in Modern. Its usual replacement, Demonic Consultation, isn't legal either, so the instant "exile your library, then win with Oracle" combo doesn't exist in this format. Thassa's Oracle is legal, though. The closest real deck is **Song of Creation**, an existing Modern deck that draws its whole library in one turn and then wins with Oracle or Jace. I took its most recent 5-0 league list and swapped one card to put Oracle in.

**The plan**
- Cast Song of Creation (4 mana: G, U, R plus 1). Every spell you cast after that draws you two cards.
- Chain cheap spells off it: Moxen and Mishra's Bauble cost 0, Tamiyo, Boomerang Basics and Repeal cost 1. You'll draw through the whole library that turn.
- Cast Thassa's Oracle (UU) to win. With an empty library, its own two blue pips are enough to beat a library of 0.
- Song makes you discard your hand at end of turn, so you need to finish the same turn. That's the same "go all-in, then win" feel that Tainted Pact gives.

**The key cards**
- **Thassa's Oracle (1 copy):** the cheapest finisher. It also wins with a few cards still left in the library if your blue devotion is high enough. It takes the slot of the list's 1 Grapeshot.
- **Jace, Wielder of Mysteries (1 copy):** backup finisher. Once the library is empty, your next draw wins instead.
- **Malevolent Rumble, Preordain, Tamiyo, Emry, Urza's Saga:** dig for Song and set it up.
- **Boomerang Basics and Repeal:** cheap spells that draw a card, so they keep the chain going under Song. They can also bounce a Mox to recast it for another two cards.
- **Endurance:** puts your graveyard on the bottom of your library. That rescues you if you've drawn everything but can't win yet, and it also fights graveyard decks.

**The mana (measured: 5,000 simulated games, compared with the real 5-0 list)**
- 20 lands. That's within one standard deviation of what the 32 recent lists run (average 19.1). The deck averages 1.4 mana per spell and has 14 zero-cost cards.
- Mulligan rate: 8.5%.
- Short on lands by turn 4: 25% of games. Flooded: 0.4%. The 25% looks bad, but the deck counts on Moxen and Saga for mana, and the simulation probably doesn't credit those fully. The real list scores exactly the same here.
- Colors working: 93% of games on turn 1, 95% by turn 3.
- Song of Creation in hand by turn 4: 51.7%. Castable by turn 4: 42%. The plain draw odds of seeing one of the 4 Songs by turn 4 on the play are 52.8%.
- In practice: you'll have a turn-4 Song about half the time and be able to cast it in a little over 40% of games. Rumble and the other dig spells raise that, but I didn't measure by how much.

**Sideboarding (my judgment, built from the recent sideboard data)**
- **Against Broodscale Combo (14.4% of the field), Devoted Druid and Amulet Titan:** bring in Consign to Memory, Pithing Needle and Unholy Heat. Take out Repeal and an Explosives.
- **Against Prowess (9.9%) and Energy:** bring in Unholy Heat, Fire Magic and Haywire Mite. Cori-Steel Cutter gives you a second way to win if they're racing hard. Cut Jace and a Boomerang Basics.
- **Against control (UW, Jeskai) and other countermagic:** bring in Pact of Negation and Swan Song to force Song or Oracle through. Take out Tormod's Crypt and Explosives.
- **Against Affinity and Eldrazi Tron:** bring in Nature's Claim, Boseiju and Haywire Mite.
- **Against Living End, Goryo's Vengeance and Dredge:** Tormod's Crypt and Endurance are already in the main deck. Add Consign to Memory.

**What kind of deck this is**
It's a **tuned** version of the Song of Creation 5-0 league list, with one change: −1 Grapeshot, +1 Thassa's Oracle. Oracle shows up in about 16% of Song lists, so this isn't new ground. It's the strongest legal home I found for the card.

**Not verified**
- I didn't measure how often the deck actually completes the full draw-out-and-win turn, only how often Song is available.
- Losing Grapeshot costs a backup win against opponents who can disrupt you mid-turn. That's my judgment, not tested.

results.prompt: I want a Modern Merfolk deck that can beat the current top decks.
results.text:
Here's a mono-blue Merfolk list. The main deck is the latest 5-0 Modern League list (dated 2026-10-13) with no changes. I only changed the sideboard, to aim it at the decks that show up most in current results.

**Main deck (60)**
4 Aether Vial, 4 Tide Shaper, 4 Lord of Atlantis, 4 Master of the Pearl Trident, 4 Silvergill Adept, 4 Vodalian Hexcatcher, 4 Harbinger of the Seas, 4 Svyelun of Sea and Sky, 4 Snapback, 4 Flare of Denial, 4 Sink into Stupor, 4 Cavern of Souls, 3 Mutavault, 2 Otawara, Soaring City, 7 Island

**Sideboard (15)**
4 Chalice of the Void, 4 Consign to Memory, 3 Force of Negation, 2 Subtlety, 2 Dismember

**The plan**
Play cheap Merfolk early, often through Aether Vial or Cavern of Souls so they're hard to counter. Then pump them with four kinds of lord and swing past blockers with islandwalk. Free interaction (Flare of Denial, Snapback, Hexcatcher sacrifices) lets you keep tapping out for creatures while still stopping the opponent's key turn.

**Why the key cards**
- **Harbinger of the Seas and Tide Shaper** turn the opponent's lands into Islands. That gives every Merfolk islandwalk from the lords and makes Tide Shaper a 2/2. Harbinger also shuts off nonbasic lands like Urza's Saga and Eldrazi Temple, which Broodscale Combo plays in every list.
- **Vodalian Hexcatcher** is a lord with flash. You can sacrifice a Merfolk to counter a noncreature spell unless they pay 1.
- **Svyelun** draws a card each time it attacks. It gives your other Merfolk ward 1 and is indestructible once you have two other Merfolk.
- **Flare of Denial and Snapback** can be cast for free (Flare by sacrificing a blue creature, Snapback by exiling a blue card). **Sink into Stupor** works as a spell or as a land, since it's a double-faced card.

**The mana (measured)**
The main deck is the same as the reference list, so the 5,000-game simulation gave identical numbers for both:
- Mulligan rate: 11.1%
- Correct colours available: 79.3% on turn 2, 88% by turn 4
- At least one lord (Lord of Atlantis, Master of the Pearl Trident or Hexcatcher) castable on turn 2: 51.3%; in hand by then: 84.8%

The deck checker counts 18 lands against the 17.4 average across 14 recent Merfolk lists. The simulation also reported a 42% "screw" rate and only 2.72 lands in play by turn 4. I think that figure is too high, because the simulator plays out mana only and ignores Aether Vial putting creatures into play. This curve tops out at 3 mana, so I didn't add lands to a proven list.

**Sideboarding against the top decks**
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%, the largest deck):** bring in Chalice on 1 (it stops Blade of the Bloodchief), Consign to Memory, Force of Negation and Subtlety. Consign counters colourless spells like Emrakul and triggered abilities. Take out Snapback and some Sink into Stupor.
- **Prowess (9.9%), Energy (6.1%), Domain Zoo (4%):** bring in Dismember and Chalice on 1. Take out Force of Negation and the slower counters. In mono-blue, Dismember costs 1 mana and 4 life.
- **Affinity (5.4%):** Chalice on 1 and Consign.
- **Eldrazi Tron (4.9%):** Chalice on 1 or 2, Force of Negation, Consign (Eldrazi are colourless spells) and Subtlety.
- **Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, Storm, Devoted Druid Combo:** Force of Negation, Consign and Subtlety (against Living End's cascade creatures). Take out Snapback.

**What I changed**
The reference sideboard had 4 Force of Negation and 3 Subtlety. I cut one of each for 2 Dismember. Creature decks make up about a quarter of the field, and the main deck has no way to kill a creature, only to bounce it. Dismember shows up in 28.6% of Merfolk sideboards.

**Not verified**
- The matchup advice is my judgment from card text and the decks' main-deck lists. I didn't test any games.
- The deck is built from 14 recent Merfolk lists, which is a small sample, so it may change faster than the bigger decks.
- I didn't add graveyard hate. Ghost Vacuum is the 1-mana option if Goryo's Vengeance and Living End become more common where you play.

intent.goal: Deliver a competitive Modern Merfolk decklist that is well-positioned against the current top decks of the metagame.

results.prompt: Make a fun mono white control deck for Modern leagues.
results.text:
I submitted the deck and it was accepted, labeled a **brew**. The main deck is the locked engine with one small change: −1 Lion Sash, +1 Path to Exile. I also swapped one sideboard card.

## The plan
This is mono-white blink control. Cheap creatures stop a threat or draw a card when they enter the battlefield (Solitude, Skyclave Apparition, Wall of Omens, Spirited Companion). Then you use Ephemerate, Restoration Angel, Flickerwisp and Phelia to exile and return them so they do it again, and you pull ahead on cards. Wrath of God resets the board when you fall behind. The Wandering Emperor, Overlord of the Mistmoors' flying insects and Solitude's lifelink close the game.

## Why the key cards
- **Solitude + Ephemerate:** this is the fun turn. You evoke Solitude for free to exile a creature. Ephemerate brings it back to exile a second one, and Ephemerate's rebound (it can be cast again for free next upkeep) gets a third. Measured: the chance of having both by turn 3 on the play is 22.4%; each one alone is 48.8%.
- **Phelia and Flickerwisp:** they repeat your enter-the-battlefield effects every turn. Phelia appears in 100% of real Blink lists and Flickerwisp in 78.4%.
- **Witch Enchanter:** it destroys an artifact or enchantment, and its back face is a land. Its targets are common: Cori-Steel Cutter (9.1% of lists), Blade of the Bloodchief (10.4%) and Affinity's artifacts.
- **Why I added Path to Exile:** Prowess (9.9% of the field) and Broodscale (14.4%) punish slow answers, and Lion Sash was the slowest card in the deck. With Path, you have at least one of 7 cheap creature answers (Solitude, March, Path) by turn 2 in 65.4% of games on the play.

## The mana (23 lands + 2 Witch Enchanter)
Simulated over 5,000 games: 16.8% mulligans, 8.7% mana screw, 2.6% flood. You make all four land drops by turn 4 in 66% of games, and white mana is available about 98–99.6% of the time on each turn.

I also tested 22 lands. It did worse on every number: 19.3% mulligans, 10.5% screw and 62% hitting four land drops. So I kept 23. The deck has many 4-drops plus a 5-drop Solitude, and Castle Ardenvale and Mishra's Factory use extra mana late in the game.

The real Blink list's numbers aren't a fair comparison. It's a three-color deck built on fetchlands at about 21.7 lands, and the simulator handles it poorly (it showed 28.4% screw).

## Sideboarding against the field
Shares are each deck's percentage of the last 30 days of results.

- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%):** +3 Clarion Conqueror, +3 Damping Sphere, +1 White Orchid Phantom. Take out the 2 Wrath of God, Path, Spirited Companions and a Wall as needed.
  - Clarion stops all of the combo's pieces: Broodscale's adapt ability, Blade's equip, and sacrificing Spawn tokens for mana.
  - Ghost Quarter and Field of Ruin can hit their Urza's Saga or Eldrazi Temple.
- **Prowess (9.9%):** +2 Celestial Purge, +2 Wrath of the Skies, +1 March. Take out the 2 Overlords and 2–3 Restoration Angels. Purge answers Cori-Steel Cutter, which is red.
- **Energy, Domain Zoo, Frog:** +2 Wrath of the Skies, plus Celestial Purge when they have red or black threats. Take out the slow cards.
- **Affinity (5.4%):** +2 Wrath of the Skies, +3 Clarion Conqueror, +1 March.

- **Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, Murktide, Rakdos Delirium:** +3 Rest in Peace.

## Weak spots
The worst matchups are probably Broodscale, Storm, Amulet Titan, Eldrazi Tron, Living End and UW Control. Those are fast combo or big-mana decks that go over the top of a deck with no counterspells. Broodscale is also the most-played deck, which is why the sideboard now has 3 Clarion Conqueror (I swapped one White Orchid Phantom for it). Wrath of God also kills your own creatures, so plan it for turns when you're behind on board.

This is a **brew**. It takes the Phelia / Flickerwisp / Solitude / Ephemerate / Witch Enchanter core and the sideboard ideas from Modern Blink, then rebuilds it as mono-white with Wall of Omens, Wrath of God and Overlord of the Mistmoors.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Clockwork Percussionist
- 4 Gingerbrute
- 4 Goblin Bushwhacker
- 4 Goblin Tomb Raider
- 4 Voldaren Epicure
- 4 Lightning Bolt
- 4 Galvanic Blast
- 2 Chain Lightning
- 1 Flame Jab
- 4 Rally at the Hornburg
- 3 Reckless Impulse
- 2 Inventor's Axe
- 2 Experimental Synthesizer
- 4 Great Furnace
- 14 Mountain

- 4 Pyroblast
- 4 Smash to Smithereens
- 4 Cleansing Wildfire
- 3 End the Festivities

**The plan**
Most of your hand costs one mana: 20 one-drop creatures, most of which can attack the turn they come down or deal damage right away. You flood the board on turns 1–2, then make a big attack with a kicked Goblin Bushwhacker or Rally at the Hornburg. Cheap burn clears blockers and finishes the opponent. The average card costs 1.17 mana, and the deck only has one- and two-drops.

**Why the key cards**
- **Goblin Bushwhacker and Rally at the Hornburg:** These win games. Kicked Bushwhacker gives your whole team +1/+0 and haste. Rally makes two 1/1s, and your Human tokens get haste.
- **Goblin Tomb Raider, Galvanic Blast and Great Furnace:** The artifacts (Furnace, Gingerbrute, Percussionist, Synthesizer, Axe) turn Tomb Raider into a 2/2 with haste. With three artifacts in play, Galvanic Blast deals 4 damage.
- **Voldaren Epicure and Clockwork Percussionist:** Epicure deals 1 damage and makes an artifact (a Blood token) when it enters. Percussionist gives you a card back when it dies.
- **Reckless Impulse and Experimental Synthesizer:** These refill your hand, so you don't run out of gas after the first big attack.

**What I changed and why**
The donor list ran 4 Burning-Tree Emissary. Its cost is red/green hybrid, so the card pool tool doesn't count it as mono-red, which breaks your red-only request. I replaced it with 2 Chain Lightning and 2 Experimental Synthesizer. Across 216 recent Rally lists, these are the two most common cards outside the core: 85% run Chain Lightning and 72% run Synthesizer. Synthesizer is also an artifact for Tomb Raider and Galvanic Blast. The cost is losing Emissary's free extra 2/2 on turn 2, which makes the turn-2 explosion a bit smaller. That's my judgment, not something I measured. If your playgroup lets hybrid cards count as red, putting the 4 Emissary back gives you the exact proven list.

**The mana (measured, 5,000 simulated games)**
- 18 lands, all red. That matches real Rally lists, which average 17.9.
- Mulligan rate: 9%. Colored mana is never a problem.
- Lands in play: about 1.8 on turn 2 and 2.5 on turn 3.
- The simulator's 32% "screw rate" counts missing your fourth land drop. Nothing in the deck costs more than 2, so that matters very little here. That's my judgment.
- The original list with Emissary simulated to the same mana numbers.

**Sideboarding (the field: Madness 16.5%, Terror 8.6%, Faeries 8.3%, Affinity 6.6%, Elves 6.3%)**
- **Faeries, Terror, Dimir Control and other blue decks:** Bring in all 4 Pyroblast. Each one counters a blue spell or destroys a blue permanent for one mana.
- **Affinity and Synthesizer:** Bring in Smash to Smithereens. It destroys an artifact and deals 3 damage to its controller.
- **Elves, Mono-White Aggro, Faeries, and token or small-creature decks:** Bring in End the Festivities. It deals 1 damage to the opponent and each of their creatures.
- **Tron, Affinity, Golgari Gardens:** Bring in Cleansing Wildfire. It destroys a land, and Affinity's lands are artifacts too, so it can hurt their metalcraft. You also draw a card.
- **What to take out:** Usually Flame Jab, Inventor's Axe and Reckless Impulse first.

**Not verified**
- How the Chain Lightning and Synthesizer swap changes your win rate isn't measured. Only the mana was simulated.
- The sideboard is the donor's, unchanged. Most Rally players also run Cast into the Fire (92%) and Relic of Progenitus (81%). If you face a lot of graveyard decks or artifact-heavy decks, consider swapping some of those in.
- The most played deck right now is a different mono-red deck, Madness, at 16.5% of the field. It's mono-red too, but it's built around Guttersnipe and burn spells more than cheap creatures. I chose Rally because you asked for creature aggro.

results.prompt: Build a Pioneer deck around Greasefang, Okiba Boss that isn't the usual list.
results.text:
I made one change after review: I swapped 2 Inspiring Vantage for 2 Starting Town. Every spell and the sideboard stay as they were. The deck has been accepted as a **brew**.

## The plan
This is a Mardu (white-black-red) Greasefang that throws vehicles into its own graveyard with red discard-and-draw spells, instead of the usual Abzan self-mill shell. On turn 2, discard a vehicle with Thrill of Possibility, Fear of Missing Out or Cathartic Reunion. On turn 3, play Greasefang. Its combat trigger brings back Parhelion II (an attack makes two 4/4 flying angels) or Detention Chariot. If the backup kill isn't needed, loop Detention Chariot every turn as removal that attacks for 6.

## Why the key cards
- **Detention Chariot:** You can discard it yourself for {W} and draw a card. When Greasefang returns it, it exiles their best blocker or artifact. The exile only lasts until the Chariot leaves play, and Greasefang sends it back to your hand at end of turn. So it clears the way for one attack each turn; it isn't permanent removal.
- **Fear of Missing Out:** It discards on entry. With four card types in your graveyard, it untaps a creature and gives you an extra combat. Greasefang's trigger reads "at the beginning of combat on your turn," so I believe it fires again in the extra combat. That's my reading of the rules text, not tested.
- **Crewing:** Greasefang has 4 power, so it can crew Parhelion II (crew 4) or the Chariot or Flagship (crew 3) by itself. Fear of Missing Out (2 power) plus Fable's 2/2 goblin can also crew, so Greasefang can attack too.
- **Can't Stay Away and Takenuma:** Both get Greasefang back after removal.

## Mana (5,000 simulated games)
| | This deck | Current stock Greasefang |
|---|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 15.1% | 16.0% |
| Too few lands | 6.9% | 6.9% |
| Too many lands | 3.7% | 3.5% |
| Right colors by turn 3 | 94.2% | 99.2% |

- **Starting Town vs. Inspiring Vantage:** With Vantage, the deck had the right colors on turn 1 in 86.5% of games and on turn 3 in 92.8%. With Starting Town, those numbers are 90.3% and 94.2%. Greasefang plus a discard spell castable by turn 3 also went up slightly, from 35.1% to 35.6%. Starting Town appears in 29 recent Greasefang lists.
- **The cost:** It's still a three-color deck, so it's about 5 points below stock on colors by turn 3.
- **Hand odds:** Greasefang and a discard spell are both in hand by turn 3 in 43.4% of games.
- **Life:** The lands cost a lot of life (shocklands, Mana Confluence, painlands, Starting Town, Multiversal Passage). That's a real problem against prowess.

## Toughest matchups
1. **Prowess (Mono-Red 10.8% + Izzet 10.8% of recent results):** They're fast, your lands cost life, and many Izzet lists sideboard Soul-Guide Lantern or Ghost Vacuum.
2. **Golgari Midrange (11.4%):** Lots of instant-speed removal (about 3.9 Fatal Push and 3.1 Abrupt Decay per list), 3.5 Graveyard Trespasser in the main deck, and Unlicensed Hearse in 84.5% of sideboards.
3. **Jund Sacrifice (9.3%):** 12.5% of lists sideboard Leyline of the Void.

## Sideboarding (my judgment, not tested)
- **Against prowess:** Bring in +2 Pest Control, +2 Lightning Helix and +1 Fatal Push. Take out −2 Thoughtseize, −2 Cathartic Reunion and −1 Can't Stay Away. Pest Control should wipe out their one-drops.
- **Against Golgari:** Bring in +2 Duress, +2 Kolaghan's Command (destroys Hearse) and +2 Vanishing Verse. Take out −2 Collective Brutality, −2 Fatal Push and −2 Cathartic Reunion. Add Loran if they show more artifact graveyard hate.
- **Against Jund Sacrifice:** Bring in +2 Pest Control, +2 Unlicensed Hearse (exiles Cauldron Familiar) and +2 Loran (answers Leyline of the Void and Witch's Oven). Take out −2 Thoughtseize, −2 Collective Brutality and −2 Bitter Triumph.
- **Against Cauldron (7.2%) and UW Control:** Bring in Duress, plus Loran and Kolaghan's Command for Agatha's Soul Cauldron. Take out some Fatal Push.
- **Against the Greasefang mirror (7%):** Bring in Unlicensed Hearse, Loran and Vanishing Verse.

## What's borrowed and what's unverified
- **Borrowed from stock Greasefang:** Greasefang, Parhelion II, Thoughtseize, Bitter Triumph, Fatal Push, Collective Brutality, Takenuma, Multiversal Passage and most of the sideboard.
- **New here:** The red discard package, Detention Chariot, Valor's Flagship and Can't Stay Away. None of those appears in recent tournament results, so the deck has no record.
- **Not checked:** I didn't look up the mana values of opponents' cards (for example Witch's Oven, Cauldron Familiar or Graveyard Trespasser). Who Pest Control and Fatal Push can hit is my assumption, and all matchup reads are judgment.

In Vintage, "artifact aggro" means Mishra's Workshop decks. Raker Shops is the most-played Workshop deck right now (9.1% of the field, 61 lists in the last 30 days), so I used its latest top-finishing list without changes.

**The plan**
Use Workshop, Ancient Tomb, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt and Grim Monolith to cast 3-mana threats on turn 1 or 2. Lock-piece artifacts like Chalice of the Void, Trinisphere and Lodestone Golem keep the opponent from catching up. Glaring Fleshraker and Scrawling Crawler deal steady damage, and Tezzeret, Mystic Forge, Time Vault and The Fantasticar can end the game quickly.

**Why the key cards**
- **Glaring Fleshraker (4):** Every colorless spell makes an Eldrazi Spawn. Every other colorless creature entering deals 1 damage to the opponent. It's in 100% of the 266 Raker Shops lists tracked.
- **Tezzeret, Cruel Captain (4):** Gains loyalty whenever an artifact enters. Its 0 untaps Grim Monolith or Time Vault, or puts a +1/+1 counter on an artifact creature. Its −3 finds a 1-mana artifact (Time Vault costs 2, so it can't find that). In 97.7% of lists.
- **Scrawling Crawler (4):** Both players draw each upkeep, and the opponent loses 1 life for each card they draw. This list's notable choice: it plays Crawler instead of The One Ring. 99.2% of Raker lists play 4 One Ring; only 32.7% play Crawler. If you'd rather have the more common card-draw build, swap 4 Crawler for 4 One Ring.
- **Sensei's Divining Top (4), Manifold Key, Time Vault:** Top smooths your draws. Key or Tezzeret untapping Time Vault takes extra turns.
- **Karn, the Great Creator:** Turns off the opponent's artifact abilities. Its −2 can fetch any artifact from your sideboard (Masticore, Null Rod, Cage, Needle, Serpent), so those count as extra copies in game 1. That's my judgment of how it plays, not a measured stat.

**The mana**
- check_deck: 18 lands, 6–7 sources of each color (Moxen and Talon Gates), average mana value 1.76. It flags 18 lands as about 3 more than the archetype average (15.4). This list counts Urza's Saga, Strip Mine and 2 Wasteland among them, and I kept it as the 5-0 list built it.
- Simulation (5,000 games):
  - Mulligans: 8.6%
  - Colors: 100% castable every turn
  - Some 3-drop threat in your opening hand by turn 2: 67.3%
  - A threat in hand plus the mana to cast it on turn 2: 26.3%
  - The tool's "screw" count: 32.8%. It only counts land drops, so I'd expect it to overstate the problem in a deck this full of fast mana (my judgment).
- Every number matched the real reference list exactly, since it's the same 60.

Stock. It's the most recent top-finishing Raker Shops list with no changes. check_deck found no errors and submit_deck accepted it.

results.text:
I've submitted a stock Golgari Midrange list for Standard: the most recent top-finishing build in the results data, with no changes.

**Before you start: this deck isn't a strong performer right now.** Golgari Midrange doesn't appear among the 20 most-played strategies in the last 30 days. The archetype tool found only 9 lists. The list I copied finished 32nd at Standard Challenge 16 (2026-10-11) with a 1–3 record. It's the most recent proven Black-Green list, but it hasn't racked up wins. If winning matters more than colors, Jund Sacrifice (11.2% of the field) and Dimir Midrange (9.7%) are the most-played decks right now.

**The deck (60 cards)**
- **Creatures (14):** 3 Environmental Scientist, 4 Simulacrum Shaper, 3 Emeritus of Abundance, 4 Vraska, the Cutting Glare
- **Planeswalkers (9):** 2 Ral Zarek, Guest Lecturer, 3 Professor Dellian Fel, 2 Garruk, Curse Breaker, 2 Garruk, Veiled Butcher
- **Removal (13):** 3 Requiting Hex, 2 Bitter Triumph, 2 Shoot the Sheriff, 4 Witherbloom Charm, 2 Maelstrom Pulse
- **Lands (24):** 4 Overgrown Tomb, 4 Wastewood Verge, 4 Deathcap Glade, 4 Ba Sing Se, 5 Swamp, 3 Forest
- **Sideboard (15):** 4 Duress, 4 Vicious Rivalry, 2 Strategic Betrayal, 2 Outrageous Robbery, 2 Ghost Vacuum, 1 Maelstrom Pulse

**The plan**
Kill the opponent's early plays with cheap removal and fetch extra lands with your creatures. Then win the long game with planeswalkers that draw cards, gain life and remove creatures. Vraska is a 4/4 deathtouch for three that later becomes a removal spell.

**Why the key cards**
- **Simulacrum Shaper and Environmental Scientist** each search out a basic land. The Shaper puts it onto the battlefield and draws a card when it dies. They help you reach your five-drop Garruks, and they help Vraska: she only destroys a permanent if you control six or more lands when she enters.
- **Removal:** Requiting Hex costs one mana but only hits creatures costing 2 or less. Shoot the Sheriff can't target outlaws (Assassins, Mercenaries, Pirates, Rogues, Warlocks). Bitter Triumph also hits planeswalkers. Witherbloom Charm can draw two cards, gain 5 life or destroy a cheap permanent. Maelstrom Pulse destroys any nonland permanent.
- **Planeswalkers:** Professor Dellian Fel can draw a card each turn, gain 3 life or destroy a creature. Garruk, Veiled Butcher makes each player sacrifice a creature or makes the opponent discard two cards. Garruk, Curse Breaker makes 4/4 creatures. Ral Zarek brings back a dead creature costing 3 or less.

**The mana (simulated over 5,000 games)**
- It runs 24 lands: 17 can make black and 19 can make green. That's slightly fewer than the archetype's average (18.2 black, 20.3 green), which the deck check didn't flag.
- You mulligan 15.9% of the time, miss land drops (screw) 7.7% of the time and flood 3.6% of the time.
- You make every land drop through turn 4 in 71.1% of games.
- You have the right colors in 83.8% of games on turn 3, rising to 91.3% on turn 4. The turn-3 dip likely comes from Vraska needing two black and Shaper needing two green.
- You average 4.85 lands on turn 6. That count ignores the land searches, so Vraska's six-land removal usually depends on Shaper or Scientist.

**Sideboarding** (these are my judgment from the card text, not tested)
- **Against creature decks (Elementals, Landfall, Prowess, Boros Dwarves):** bring in Vicious Rivalry. It destroys every artifact and creature costing up to the life you pay. Take out Maelstrom Pulse and the Ral Zareks.
- **Against Dimir Midrange, 4C Control and Azorius Control:** bring in Duress and Outrageous Robbery, plus Strategic Betrayal against Dimir. Take out Requiting Hex, then Shoot the Sheriff against creature-light builds.
- **Against Reanimator:** bring in Strategic Betrayal, which exiles their whole graveyard, and Ghost Vacuum. Garruk, Veiled Butcher also helps by exiling their creatures instead of letting them die. Take out Requiting Hex.

results.prompt: Make a Legacy deck that wins on turn 1 every game.
results.text:
It can't be done: no Legacy deck wins on turn 1 every game. Your opening seven is random, half your games you're on the draw, and opponents can stop you with Force of Will, discard or graveyard hate. The closest real thing is a proven Oops All Spells list, which is built to win on turn 1 as often as possible. I submitted it without changes.

**The plan**
The deck has no cards that count as lands while they're in the library. Its only lands are the back faces of double-faced spells (Boggart Trawler, Fell the Profane, Agadeem's Awakening), and in the library those count as spells. Balustrade Spy says to reveal cards "until they reveal a land card," so if you target yourself, it mills your whole library (my reading of the rules). Each Narcomoeba milled this way can come straight onto the battlefield. Then you flash back Dread Return from the graveyard by sacrificing three creatures, and return Thassa's Oracle. With your library empty, Oracle wins the game.

**Why these cards**
- **Mana without lands:** Dark Ritual and Cabal Ritual (each adds {B}{B}{B}), Lotus Petal, Chrome Mox, and the two Spirit Guides, which you exile from your hand for mana. Spy costs {3}{B}, so these are how you reach 4 mana on turn 1.
- **Lively Dirge:** a backup way to start the combo. For 5 mana it puts Spy from your library into your graveyard, then returns it to play, which triggers the mill.
- **Agadeem's Awakening:** brings creatures back from your graveyard, or you can play it as a land.
- **Protection:** Thoughtseize, Duress and Cabal Therapy strip counterspells from the opponent's hand before you go off. Pact of Negation costs 0 and counters a spell, but you must pay {3}{U}{U} at your next upkeep or lose. That's fine if you win this turn and fatal if the combo fizzles.

**Honest odds** (exact draw math, 7 cards, no mulligans)
- **Turn 1, strictest line:** Spy + Dark Ritual + a double-faced land + a Spirit Guide in your opening hand: **5.4%**.
- **Turn 1, looser estimate:** Spy or Dirge + any Ritual + a black source + one extra mana: **27%**. This overcounts: Lotus Petal counts in two groups, Dirge needs 5 mana and Cabal Ritual costs 2. A real turn-1 win rate is probably 15–25%, before the opponent interacts.
- **By turn 2:** enabler + Ritual + black source: **44.2%**.

**The mana**
The deck has 0 real lands, the same as the tournament lists of this deck. The deck checker's warning to "add 14 lands" doesn't apply here: real lands in the library would stop Spy partway through. Thassa's Oracle is always brought back from the graveyard, never cast, so the blue-source warning doesn't matter either. The simulator can't model this deck. It treats every hand as a mulligan because it doesn't count Rituals or Spirit Guides as mana, so its numbers aren't meaningful, and I used exact draw math instead.

**Sideboarding** (my judgment)
- **Against graveyard hate:** bring in the second plan, 4 Goblin Charbelcher, 4 Lion's Eye Diamond, 4 Beseech the Mirror and 2 Chrome Mox. With no lands in the library, Charbelcher reveals your whole library and deals that much damage, so it doesn't need the graveyard. Cut some Narcomoeba, Dread Return, Agadeem's Awakening and Lively Dirge.
- **Against the blue tempo decks** (Dimir Tempo is the biggest deck at 10.2%, Izzet Tempo 4.6%): keep all the discard. Cast Thoughtseize or Duress before you try to win.
- **Against fast combo** (Doomsday, OmniTell, Sneak and Show): just race them, using discard as needed.
- **Against Ocelot Aggro and Eldrazi Aggro:** speed is your main weapon. Fell the Profane can also kill a key creature.

**Label:** Stock. This is the most recent top-finishing Oops All Spells list (23rd place, 3-3, Legacy Challenge 32). It's a small deck: 17 tournament lists in the last 90 days.

**Not checked by any tool:** the turn-1 win rate once opponents interact. That depends on how often they hold Force of Will or graveyard hate, and no tool here measures it.

results.prompt: Build a Timeless reanimator deck.
results.text:
# Timeless BR Reanimator (adapted from Legacy, so labelled "tuned")

**Where this list comes from:** There's no tournament data for Timeless yet. The meta tool pointed me to Legacy, where Reanimator has 214 recent lists. I used the most common build there, black-red with Dark Ritual and Faithless Looting. Then I checked every card for Timeless legality and replaced the ones that aren't legal. **This exact 60 has not put up results. It's a proven shell with substitutions, not a list that has won anything.**

## The plan
Get a huge creature into your graveyard on turn 1 or 2 with Entomb, Faithless Looting, Troll's swampcycling or Collective Brutality's discard cost. Then return it with Reanimate, Necromancy or Persist. Before you go off, use Thoughtseize and Grief to take away their answer.

## Main deck (60)
**Creatures (17)**
- 4 Griselbrand
- 3 Atraxa, Grand Unifier
- 2 Sire of Seven Deaths
- 2 Troll of Khazad-dûm
- 1 Raph & Mikey, Troublemakers
- 3 Grief

**Spells (26)**
- 4 Entomb
- 4 Reanimate
- 4 Necromancy
- 2 Persist
- 4 Faithless Looting
- 4 Dark Ritual
- 4 Thoughtseize
- 2 Collective Brutality

**Lands (17)**
- 4 Bloodstained Mire
- 2 Verdant Catacombs
- 2 Polluted Delta
- 4 Blood Crypt
- 1 Raucous Theater
- 4 Swamp

## Why these cards
- **Reanimate and Entomb** are the same core as Legacy. Entomb is legal in Timeless and puts any creature straight into your graveyard for one mana. Oddly, it didn't show up in the Legacy data, so playing 4 is my call.
- **Necromancy** replaces Animate Dead, which isn't legal in Timeless. It costs 3 instead of 2, but Dark Ritual can still make it a turn-1 play.
- **Persist** returns Sire of Seven Deaths, Troll or Grief. It can't return Griselbrand or Atraxa because they're legendary, so I only play 2.
- **Griselbrand and Atraxa** come from Legacy (93% and 99% of lists run them). They refill your hand right away.
- **Sire of Seven Deaths** replaces Archon of Cruelty, which isn't legal. It's a 7/7 with lifelink and ward that costs 7 life to target, and it can be returned with Persist.
- **Troll** works as a discard outlet: swampcycling for {1} fetches you a land and puts Troll in the graveyard. It's also a fine creature to reanimate.
- **Grief** replaces Unmask and Cabal Therapy, which aren't legal. Exiling a black card to play it for free, then Reanimating it, gives you two discard effects on turn 1.

**Other Legacy staples that aren't legal in Timeless:** Lotus Petal, Shallow Grave, Exhume, Goryo's Vengeance, Underground Sea and Badlands.

## Mana (simulated over 5,000 games)
- **Mulligan rate:** 9.6%.
- **Turn 2:** you have both a way to fill the graveyard and a reanimation spell in hand 63% of the time. You can actually cast both by turn 2 36.5% of the time.
- **Colours:** you have the colours you need on turn 1 82% of the time, rising to 90% on turn 2. Red for Faithless Looting is the usual problem.
- **Land count:** check_deck recommends about 23 lands. That number is skewed because it treats the ten 7–8 mana creatures as cards you'll cast. Legacy lists average 14.6 lands plus Lotus Petal. Without Petal I went to 17. The simulator's "screw" rate of 37% measures falling behind on land drops through turn 4, which this deck doesn't need. In my judgment it isn't a real weakness here.

## Sideboard (15)
Without Timeless data, these are standard plans by type of opponent:
- **Graveyard hate (Leyline of the Void, Tormod's Crypt, Endurance):** bring in 2 Duress and 1 Collective Brutality, and cast your discard before you commit. Sire and Troll can also just be hard-cast if you have a lot of mana.
- **Blue counterspell decks (Force of Will, Force of Negation):** bring in Duress and Dauthi Voidwalker. Make them use counterspells on your discard spells first.
- **Other graveyard decks, or the mirror:** bring in 2 Surgical Extraction and 3 Dauthi Voidwalker.
- **Fast creature decks:** bring in 2 Fatal Push and 2 Abrade.
- **Artifact decks:** bring in Abrade and Meltdown.
- **Decks relying on lots of nonbasic lands (multicolour control):** bring in 2 Blood Moon. Your 4 basic Swamps and fetches let you play around it.

For each, cut Persist, a Raph & Mikey or a Collective Brutality first.

## Not checked
- None of these card choices have been tested in Timeless results.
- Sire of Seven Deaths in place of Archon, 4 Entomb and 17 lands are my judgment calls.
- I haven't confirmed which decks are popular on Arena right now, so treat the sideboard as a general plan rather than one tuned to the current metagame.

results.prompt: Make an Elves deck for Historic.
results.text:
I couldn't find a proven Historic Elves list to give you. The database has no Historic tournament results. The closest formats with data are Pioneer and Standard, and neither has an Elves deck in its recent results. So this is a **brew**: a Golgari Elves list I built from cards the tool confirmed are Historic-legal, then checked with the deck checker and the simulator. It isn't copied from any tournament list.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Elvish Mystic, 3 Allosaurus Shepherd
- 4 Elvish Warmaster, 4 Leaf-Crowned Visionary, 4 Elvish Clancaller
- 4 Elvish Archdruid, 2 Marwyn, the Nurturer, 3 Elderfang Ritualist
- 2 Lathril, Blade of the Elves
- 4 Collected Company
- 4 Overgrown Tomb, 3 Woodland Cemetery, 2 Llanowar Wastes, 2 Skemfar Elderhall, 1 Castle Garenbrig, 10 Forest

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Thoughtseize, 3 Fatal Push
- 2 Reclamation Sage, 2 Pelakka Predation
- 2 Poison-Tip Archer, 2 Dwynen, Gilt-Leaf Daen
- 1 Elderfang Ritualist

**The plan**
Play a mana elf on turn 1, a 2-mana Elf that pumps your team on turn 2, then dump your hand with Elvish Archdruid or Marwyn. You win by attacking with a wide board of boosted Elves, or by tapping ten Elves with Lathril so the opponent loses 10 life. Collected Company refills the board at instant speed. It can only find creatures costing 3 or less, and 36 of your 38 creatures qualify (all but Lathril).

**Why these cards**
- **Mana:** Llanowar Elves, Elvish Mystic, Archdruid (one green per Elf) and Marwyn (makes green equal to her power, which grows as Elves enter) power out fast starts.
- **Team pumps:** Clancaller, Leaf-Crowned Visionary and Archdruid each give your other Elves +1/+1, so they stack. Visionary also draws a card for {G} whenever you cast an Elf.
- **Tokens:** Warmaster makes a 1/1 Elf once each turn that another Elf enters.
- **Value and protection:**
  - Elderfang Ritualist returns another Elf to your hand when it dies, which helps against removal.
  - Allosaurus Shepherd makes your green spells uncounterable.
  - Skemfar Elderhall is a land you can sacrifice later for removal plus two Elf tokens.

**The mana (simulated over 5,000 games)**
- With 22 lands, you miss land drops (screw) 10.5% of the time and mulligan 19.3% of the time. A mana elf and a pump creature are castable by turn 3 in 95.3% of games.
- I tested 21 lands too. That cut the mulligan rate to 8.7% but doubled the screw rate to 21.8%, so I kept 22. The checker suggests about 20.5 lands. If you'd rather lean on the mana elves, cut a Forest.
- With 8 one-mana elves, you have one in your opening hand 65.4% of the time.
- There are 9 black sources. The right color is available about 91–94% of the time from turn 3 on.

**Sideboarding**
I have no Historic results, so I don't know what the field looks like. This is general advice, not based on data:
- **Against control or counterspell decks:** bring in Thoughtseize, Pelakka Predation and the 3rd Elderfang. Cut Marwyn and one Lathril.
- **Against aggro and creature decks:** bring in Fatal Push, Poison-Tip Archer and Dwynen (she gains life when she attacks with your Elves). Cut Visionary and one Allosaurus Shepherd.
- **Against artifact or enchantment decks:** bring in Reclamation Sage.
- **Against mass removal ("wipe the board" spells):** keep Collected Company and Elderfang, and don't overextend.

**Not verified**
- I couldn't test how this deck performs against real opponents, because there's no Historic data.
- The card choices and counts are my judgment, based on what Historic Elves decks have looked like before. They haven't been confirmed by recent results.

results.prompt: Build an Old School 93/94 control deck.
results.text:
I couldn't hand you a proven list. The tools have no tournament results for Old School, and the nearest format they suggest is Premodern, which has a different card pool. So this is my own build of the classic Old School control deck, "The Deck," in blue-white with a red splash. I submitted it as a brew, not stock. I checked every card's text and Old School legality, and the deck passes the legality check, but its card choices are my judgment, not borrowed from a winning list.

## The deck (60)

**Lands (19):** 1 Library of Alexandria, 2 Mishra's Factory, 1 Strip Mine, 4 Tundra, 3 Volcanic Island, 1 Plateau, 2 City of Brass, 5 Island
**Fast mana (6):** Black Lotus, Mox Sapphire, Mox Pearl, Mox Ruby, Mox Jet, Sol Ring
**Card draw and power (6):** Ancestral Recall, Time Walk, Timetwister, Braingeyser, Recall, 2 Jayemdae Tome
**Counterspells (7):** Mana Drain, 4 Counterspell, 2 Red Elemental Blast
**Removal and answers (14):** 4 Swords to Plowshares, 3 Disenchant, Balance, Chaos Orb, Moat, 3 Lightning Bolt, Psionic Blast
**Ways to win and stay alive (8):** 2 Serendib Efreet, 2 Serra Angel, Fireball, Mirror Universe, Ivory Tower

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Blue Elemental Blast, 1 Red Elemental Blast, 1 Moat, 1 Circle of Protection: Red, 2 Divine Offering, 1 Energy Flux, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 1 Control Magic, 1 Power Sink, 1 Serra Angel, 1 Strip Mine

## The plan
Trade one-for-one early with Swords, Bolt, Disenchant and counters. Then pull ahead on cards with Library of Alexandria, Jayemdae Tome, Ancestral Recall and Braingeyser while Moat and Balance stop the creature decks. Win with Serra Angels, Serendib Efreets, Factories or a big Fireball, or swap life totals with Mirror Universe once you're low.

## Key cards
- **Mana Drain and 4 Counterspell:** your main defense. Mana Drain also gives you colorless mana on your next turn, which pays for Tome or Fireball.
- **Moat:** non-flying creatures can't attack, but your flyers still can.
- **Balance:** a cheap reset, and it works best when you hold few cards and have few creatures.
- **Recall:** gets back restricted cards like Ancestral Recall or Time Walk.
- **Ivory Tower:** gains life while you sit on a full hand for Library.
- **The red cards:** Bolt, Fireball and Psionic Blast kill creatures and finish games. Red Elemental Blast in the main deck is for the blue mirror match.
- **Mox Jet:** only there as an extra zero-cost mana source. The deck has no black spells.

## Mana (5,000 simulated games)
- Coloured sources: 16 blue, 9 white, 8 red.
- My first draft had 18 lands with 3 Strip Mine and 3 Factory. It came out badly: 34.1% of games short on lands and 46–59% of hands able to pay the right colours. I cut down the colourless lands, went to 19 lands, and cut Power Sink to the sideboard.
- **Final numbers:** 8.6% mulligans, 29.8% short on lands, 0.3% flooded. About 3.0 lands in play on turn 4. The right colours were available 56% of the time on turn 2 and 65% on turn 4.
- **That's still shaky.** The simulator probably counts a hand as bad whenever Serra Angel's double white or a red card isn't castable yet, and it may undercount the Moxen and Sol Ring. Even so, the deck checker recommends about 20.7 lands. **If you keep stumbling, swap a Mishra's Factory for a Tundra or a fourth Volcanic Island.**

## Sideboarding (judgment; there's no matchup data)
- **Red burn or aggro:** bring in 3 Blue Elemental Blast, Circle of Protection: Red and the second Moat. Take out the 2 Red Elemental Blast, Mirror Universe and Braingeyser.
- **Blue control mirror:** bring in the third Red Elemental Blast, Power Sink and Control Magic. Take out Moat and 1–2 Swords.
- **Artifact decks (Shops, Robots):** bring in 2 Divine Offering and Energy Flux. Take out Moat and Swords if they have few creatures. Disenchant already helps here.
- **Graveyard decks (Animate Dead, Reanimator):** bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt.
- **Land-based decks (e.g. Library or Mishra's Workshop):** bring in the second Strip Mine.

## Assumptions and what isn't verified
- **Restricted list:** I used the Old School restricted list in the tool, which may follow one specific ruleset. Check your local rules, especially if Strip Mine or Mishra's Factory should be restricted. Chaos Orb also needs your playgroup to allow the physical flip.
- **Not tested in play:** none of the matchup advice or card counts (Moat, the Bolts, Mirror Universe) has been tested against real Old School results. It's based on how the archetype traditionally plays.

results.prompt: Make a Penny Dreadful burn deck.
results.text:
**Mono-Red Burn for Penny Dreadful (a brew, not a proven list)**

You asked for a proven deck, but I couldn't find one to copy. My tools have no tournament results for Penny Dreadful. The closest formats with data, Pauper and Modern, don't have a burn deck in their recent results. Many of the usual burn cards are also banned here: I checked Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, Lava Spike, Rift Bolt, Goblin Guide, Monastery Swiftspear, Eidolon of the Great Revel, Fireblast, Skewer the Critics and Lightning Helix, and none are legal. So I built the classic mono-red burn layout (cheap hasty threats, about 20 burn spells, 20 lands) from cards I confirmed are legal in Penny Dreadful. That makes it a **brew**, not tested in tournaments.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Vexing Devil
- 4 Scorch Spitter
- 4 Viashino Pyromancer
- 4 Keldon Marauders
- 2 Bonecrusher Giant
- 4 Burst Lightning
- 4 Shock
- 4 Lightning Strike
- 4 Searing Spear
- 2 Magma Jet
- 2 Exquisite Firecraft
- 2 Sulfuric Vortex
- 17 Mountain
- 2 Castle Embereth
- 1 Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Smash to Smithereens
- 3 Pyroclasm
- 3 Rampaging Ferocidon
- 2 Price of Progress
- 2 Mizzium Mortars
- 2 Leyline of Punishment

**The plan:** Do 8–10 damage in the first turns with creatures that hurt the opponent just by entering or attacking. Then finish with burn spells aimed at their face. Use burn on creatures only when a blocker or a lifegain creature would stop you.

**Why these cards**
- **Vexing Devil:** a 1-mana card that is either 4 damage or a 4/3 body. The opponent picks, and both are good for you.
- **Scorch Spitter:** deals 1 damage to the opponent every time it attacks, so it chips in even when blocked.
- **Viashino Pyromancer:** 2 damage to the opponent when it enters. Keldon Marauders deals 1 when it enters and 1 when it leaves, plus whatever it hits for as a 3/3.
- **The burn spells:** Burst Lightning and Shock are 1-mana instants. Lightning Strike and Searing Spear do 3 at instant speed. Magma Jet adds scry 2 to dig for more burn. Exquisite Firecraft does 4 and can't be countered once you have two instants or sorceries in the graveyard.
- **Bonecrusher Giant:** Stomp is 2 damage that can't be prevented, and later you get a 4/3 body.
- **Sulfuric Vortex:** 2 damage to each player every upkeep, and nobody can gain life. It shuts off lifegain decks.
- **Castle Embereth and Sokenzan:** lands that give late-game damage when you draw extra lands. Castle Embereth enters untapped if you control a Mountain.

**Mana (simulated over 5,000 games)**
- 20 lands, all making red, so you never run short of red mana (100% across the simulated turns).
- You mulligan about 8.4% of hands, and floods are rare (0.5%).
- The tool flags 25.6% of games as land-short. Its checker suggests about 23 lands. I stayed at 20 because the average card costs only 1.75 and nothing costs more than 3. Burn wants to draw spells, not lands. If you find you stall on two lands, cut a Magma Jet for a 21st Mountain.
- By turn 2, the measured chance of having both a 1-drop creature and a 2-drop creature in hand is 47.6%, and 38.3% that both are castable. Burn fills the gaps.

**Sideboarding** (my judgment, since there's no field data)
- **Artifact decks:** bring in Smash to Smithereens. It destroys an artifact and deals 3 damage to its controller.
- **Wide token or creature decks:** bring in Pyroclasm, which deals 2 to every creature, and Mizzium Mortars. Take out Scorch Spitter and Sulfuric Vortex.
- **Lifegain decks:** bring in Rampaging Ferocidon, Leyline of Punishment and the extra Vortex effects. All of them stop lifegain.
- **Decks with lots of nonbasic lands:** bring in Price of Progress. Penny mana bases are often mostly basics, so check the opponent first.

**Not checked**
- Penny Dreadful's legal card pool changes every season. Everything above was legal when I checked, but confirm before you play.
- I found no legal graveyard removal among the cards I tried, so the sideboard has none.
- How this deck would match up against specific Penny decks is a guess, not a measurement.

I made 2 main-deck changes and 4 sideboard changes. Your list is card-for-card the same as the most recent top UB Psychatog result (4th place, Premodern Challenge 16), so it's already a proven shell. The changes only aim it at the decks showing up most right now.

**The plan (unchanged):** Counter and discard their key spells, draw cards with Gush, Accumulated Knowledge and Fact or Fiction, and keep the graveyard full. Then Psychatog wins in one or two big attacks. Smother, Sickening Dreams and Powder Keg handle the cheap creatures.

## Main deck changes
- **Out: 1 Lim-Dûl's Vault, 1 Thwart. In: 2 Annul.**
  - **Why Annul:** The current top four are Enchantress (12.5%), Terrageddon (11.2%), Stiflenought (10.4%) and Sligh (9.9%). Annul does real work against three of them:
    - Against Enchantress, nearly every key card is an enchantment: Enchantress's Presence, Wild Growth, Parallax Wave, Opalescence, Solitary Confinement.
    - Against Stiflenought, it counters Phyrexian Dreadnought, which is an artifact.
    - Against Sligh, it counters Sulfuric Vortex, Pyrostatic Pillar, Cursed Scroll and Black Vise.
    - It's also the most common main-deck flex card in Tog lists (53%).
  - **Why those two cuts:** They're the least played cards in the list. Vault appears in 13.6% of Tog lists and Thwart in 3.4%. Vault is slow and gains you no cards. Thwart is mostly a Stiflenought card.
- **What I left alone:** The 20 lands and the rest of the spells. You run 17 blue and 9 black sources, which matches real lists (17.15 and 8.59 on average, 19.9 lands). Your card-draw package and 4 Counterspell / 4 Foil / 3 Duress are all at standard numbers.

## Mana (measured, 5,000 simulated games)
- Mulligan rate: 8.4%.
- Missed a land drop by turn 4: 24.5%.
- Flood: 0.5%.
- Both colors available by turn 3: 80.2%.

These numbers are effectively the same as the reference list, since the lands didn't change. The checker suggests 22 lands, but real Tog lists run about 20 because Gush and the cantrips make up for it. I kept 20 on that evidence.

## Sideboard changes
- **Out:** Morphling, 1 Chain of Vapor, 1 Engineered Plague, 1 Annul (moved to the main deck).
- **In:** 2 Tormod's Crypt, 1 Tsabo's Web, 1 Powder Keg.
- **Why:**
  - **Tormod's Crypt:** You had no fast graveyard hate. Hermit Druid Combo (5.5%) runs Animate Dead, Unearth and Shallow Grave. Replenish is 4.8%, Enchantress runs about 2 Replenish, and the Tog mirror is 4.8%. Crypt costs 0, and 46.6% of Tog sideboards run it.
  - **Tsabo's Web:** In 80.7% of Tog sideboards. It locks down Terrageddon's Rishadan Port, Wasteland and Treetop Village, plus Sligh's Mishra's Factory and Barbarian Ring. It also draws a card.
  - **Second Powder Keg:** Clears 1-drops (Dreadnought, Jackal Pup, Mogg Fanatic, Lavamancer, Wild Growth) and 2-drops (Argothian Enchantress, Seal of Cleansing).
  - **Engineered Plague, down to 1:** The tribal decks it beats are now small. Goblins is only 4.4%.

## Sideboard guide (which cards to bring in and take out is my judgment)
- **Enchantress:**
  - In: Annul, 2 Back to Basics (they play 4 Serra's Sanctum, 4 Brushland and fetch lands), Crypt (for Replenish).
  - Out: 3 Smother (Argothian Enchantress can't be targeted), Sickening Dreams.
  - Expect them to bring in Xantid Swarm and Tormod's Crypt against you.
- **Terrageddon:**
  - In: 2 Back to Basics, Tsabo's Web, Control Magic (steal Terravore).
  - Out: Duress, Chain of Vapor, Annul.
  - Save Counterspell for Armageddon and Terravore. Nimble Mongoose can't be targeted, so Smother can't hit it.
- **Stiflenought:**
  - In: Annul, Duress, Powder Keg, Control Magic.
  - Out: Sickening Dreams, 1–2 Smother.
  - Don't bring Hydroblast or Blue Elemental Blast. They only hit red cards, and Stiflenought is mono-blue.
- **Sligh and Goblins:**
  - In: 2 Hydroblast, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, Powder Keg, Plague (Goblins only).
  - Out: Duress, Fact or Fiction, Chain of Vapor, Gush (Gush puts lands back in your hand, which is risky when they're burning you out).
- **Hermit Druid and Replenish:**
  - In: 2 Crypt, Annul (against Survival of the Fittest), Duress, Back to Basics (Druid plays almost no basic lands), Haunting Echoes.

results.text:
I made one change, to the mana base, and the revised deck was accepted. It's a **brew**: it uses the Living End shell and adds Scam's evoke creatures.

## The plan
On turns 1–2, cycle the big creatures into your graveyard, or evoke an Incarnation to disrupt the opponent and leave a creature in the graveyard. On turn 3, cast Shardless Agent, Violent Outburst or Demonic Dread. Cascade can only hit Living End, because every other nonland card costs 3 or more. Living End brings everything back as 5/5s and 6/5s, and you win in one or two attacks.

## Why these cards
- **Grief and Fury are banned**, so the Incarnations do Scam's job. Only Subtlety and Endurance are truly free to evoke (you exile a card from your hand). Deceit, Wistfulness and Vibrance each cost two hybrid mana to evoke, and Shriekmaw costs {1}{B}. Deceit's discard mode only works if you pay it with BB.
- **Scam's 1-mana spells (Ephemerate, Undying Malice) are left out on purpose.** Cascade would hit them instead of Living End.
- **Force of Negation** protects the combo from opposing combo decks and control, for free on the opponent's turn.

## The weak spots I found
- **Graveyard hate:** Broodscale Combo is the biggest deck in the field (14.4%). 96% of its lists run Soul-Guide Lantern in the main deck, and 93% have Grafdigger's Cage in the sideboard.
- **Devoted Druid Combo** (5.1%) runs Endurance in 414 recent lists, which can shuffle your graveyard away.
- **Fast combo** like Storm and Goryo's Vengeance (3.7% each).
- **Demonic Dread** has no recent tournament results. It's untested and needs both black and red.

## The mana
- **The change:** I swapped Ziatora's Proving Ground for a second Ketria Triome. Shardless Agent and Violent Outburst need green with blue or red, and Ketria makes all three.
- **Colour sources:** 17 lands giving U 10 / B 8 / R 8 / G 11, plus 4 cyclers that fetch a land (Troll, Generous Ent). Three of the lands enter tapped.
- **Simulation (5,000 games):**
  - Mulligan rate: 9.6%.
  - Right colours on turn 3: 84.7%, up from 83.3% before the swap; the top recent Living End list gets 86.8%.
  - A cascade spell in hand by turn 3: 81.7%.
  - Castable on turn 3: only 38.3%.
- **Why that last number is low:** the simulator doesn't count fetching lands with Troll or Ent, so it plays only 2.39 lands by turn 3 on average. Under the same model, the real Living End list misses land drops more often than this one (42% vs 37.4%).
- **What I couldn't change:** I also wanted to switch to 3 Generous Ent and 1 Troll. That pushed the list over 60% identical to an existing Living End list, which a brew isn't allowed to be, so it stays at 3 Troll and 1 Ent.

## Sideboarding (my judgment, not tested)
- **Broodscale:** bring in 2 Force of Vigor, 2 Foundation Breaker and 2 Brotherhood's End (the artifact mode answers Cage, Lantern and Blade). Take out Vibrance, 2 Curator, 2 Shriekmaw and 1 Deceit.
- **Prowess / Energy / Domain Zoo:** bring in 2 Brotherhood's End and 2 Dismember. Take out 3 Force of Negation and 1 Subtlety.
- **Affinity:** bring in Force of Vigor, Foundation Breaker and Brotherhood's End. Take out 2 Shriekmaw (it can't kill artifact creatures) and some Force of Negation.
- **Storm / Goryo's:** bring in 4 Mystical Dispute and the third Endurance. Take out 2 Shriekmaw, Vibrance and 2 Curator.
- **Eldrazi Tron / Amulet Titan / UW Control:** bring in Mystical Dispute and Inevitable Betrayal. Inevitable Betrayal costs 0, so cascade can hit it instead of Living End. Only bring in both copies if you need them.
- **Devoted Druid:** bring in 2 Dismember for Curators. Use Force of Negation or Subtlety only where your copy says they hit something.

## Not checked
- I didn't measure any matchup win rates.
- The sideboard plans and the Demonic Dread package are untested.
- Living End also brings back the opponent's dead creatures. Keep that in mind against creature decks.

results.prompt: Build a Pauper deck around Kiln Fiend.
results.text:
# Mono-Red Kiln Fiend (Pauper)

**Plan:** Play Kiln Fiend or Festival Crasher on turn 2. Then cast a burst of cheap and free instants. Each one gives Kiln Fiend +3/+0 and the other two creatures +2/+0. Finish with Temur Battle Rage or Assault Strobe so a pumped creature with double strike deals 20 in one attack, usually on turn 3–4. If you have no double strike, Fireblast and Lightning Bolt are extra damage and also extra pump triggers.

## Why the key cards
- **Kiln Fiend ×4, Festival Crasher ×4, Ghitu Amplifier ×2:** 10 two-mana creatures that grow from spells. Festival Crasher's 3 toughness survives Lava Dart and Gut Shot, the pingers Madness runs.
- **Free and cheap spells:** Gut Shot and Mutagenic Growth can be paid with life instead of mana. Manamorphose replaces its own mana and draws a card. Lava Dart can be cast a second time by sacrificing a Mountain. Fireblast is free if you sacrifice two Mountains. All of them pump your creature without slowing you down.
- **Apostle's Blessing ×4, Mutagenic Growth ×4:** protection. Apostle's Blessing answers single-target removal like Snuff Out and Cast Down, which Faeries plays.
- **Lightning Bolt ×4, Fireblast ×4:** these are the only slots I could change (the rest of the deck was fixed), and I kept them. Bolt kills Madness's main creatures (Sneaky Snacker, Guttersnipe). Fireblast gives 4 free damage when you can't find double strike.

## Mana (simulated over 5,000 games, on the play)
- **Lands:** 17 Snow-Covered Mountains. The existing Kiln Fiend lists also run exactly 17 Mountains.
- **Mulligans and land drops:** you mulligan 9.6% of hands, against 10% for the real Kiln Fiend list. The "screw" figure is 37.4% against the reference's 35.7%. It looks high because the deck is built to function on two or three lands.
- **Weakest point:** there are only 5 double-strike cards (3 Battle Rage, 2 Strobe).
  - You see a creature plus a double-strike card by turn 3 on the play 46% of the time, and by turn 4 on the draw 57.1%.
  - You have creature, double strike and a protection spell all in hand and castable by turn 3 only 23.5% of the time.
  - The tournament lists run 4 Battle Rage and often 3 Strobe. The engine was fixed at this stage, so I couldn't add more. That's another reason Fireblast stays in as a backup finisher.

## What I changed (sideboard only)
- **Out:** 3 Red Elemental Blast and 2 Relic of Progenitus.
- **In:** 4 Pyroblast and 1 End the Festivities.
- **Why:** blue decks are the largest share of the field. Terror is 8.6%, Faeries 8.3%, Dimir Control 5.2%, plus some Jeskai and UW Control. Counterspell and Spellstutter Sprite are your worst enemies, so a fourth blue-hate card matters more than graveyard hate. My judgment is that Relic had little to do here.

## Sideboarding
- **Madness (16.5%, the most-played deck, a bad matchup):** bring in Electrickery and End the Festivities for Snacker, Epicure and Faerie tokens. Take out Assault Strobe and an Apostle's Blessing. Lean on Crasher's 3 toughness.
- **Terror, Faeries, Dimir Control:** bring in 4 Pyroblast. Take out Gut Shot (keep it against Faeries for 1/1 flyers) or Fireblast. Try to win the turn they tap out.
- **Affinity (6.6%):** bring in Raze the Effigy. It destroys an artifact, or gives an attacker +2/+2. Bring in Electrickery too.
- **Elves (6.3%):** bring in Electrickery and End the Festivities.
- **Mono-White Aggro:** bring in Flaring Pain to beat damage-prevention effects. Bring in Electrickery for the small creatures.
- **Tron (4.9%):** bring in Molten Rain.
- **Bogles (5.3%):** your sideboard has nothing that answers hexproof, so just race them.

## Label and what's unverified
- **Label:** this is a **brew**. It borrows its shell from the existing Kiln Fiend archetype (9 lists). It differs by playing Gut Shot, Bolt and Fireblast instead of Rite of Flame and Crash Through.
- **Not measured:** the matchup notes are my judgment from the tournament lists, not tested win rates.
- **Not tool-checked:**
  - I assumed Snow-Covered Mountain counts as a Mountain for Lava Dart's and Fireblast's sacrifice costs.
  - Fireblast leaves you weak against Molten Rain or a long game. Swapping it for Rite of Flame (the reference lists' choice) would give more spell chains but no backup damage. That trade isn't measured.
