results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
# Mono-Blue Dream Halls: wins with fliers and extra turns, not storm (Premodern brew)

**The plan:** Get Dream Halls onto the battlefield. Show and Tell can put it in play on turn 3, or you can hard-cast it with Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors and Frantic Search's untaps. Once it's down, every spell in the deck is blue, so you can cast any of them for free by discarding another blue card. Use Opportunity to draw more cards. Then cast Morphling and/or Palinchron plus Time Stretch or Time Warp, and attack with fliers through the extra turns. No storm, no Brain Freeze.

## Decklist (submitted and accepted as a brew)
**Main (60)**
- **Engine:** 4 Dream Halls, 4 Show and Tell, 3 Intuition, 4 Frantic Search, 3 Opportunity
- **Win cards:** 3 Time Stretch, 2 Time Warp, 3 Morphling, 2 Palinchron
- **Support:** 4 Impulse, 3 Merchant Scroll, 2 Mana Leak, 1 Arcane Denial, 1 Chain of Vapor
- **Lands (21):** 12 Island, 4 Ancient Tomb, 2 City of Traitors, 2 Svyelunite Temple, 1 Saprazzan Skerry

**Sideboard (15):** 2 Hydroblast, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, 2 Chill, 1 Chain of Vapor, 2 Defense Grid, 1 Stifle, 2 Teferi's Response, 1 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Annul

## What I changed in review, and why
I compared the deck against the top of the field: Enchantress 12.5%, Terrageddon 11.2%, Stiflenought 10.4%, Sligh 9.9%.
- **Enchantress was mislabeled as a good matchup.** Its lists run Solitary Confinement in 99.6% of builds (1.8 copies on average), which prevents all damage to its player. Seal of Cleansing (3.1 copies) also kills Dream Halls. Since you win with damage, Confinement alone can lock you out. **I cut a Mana Leak for 1 Chain of Vapor main.** Merchant Scroll fetches it, and so does Intuition. Bounce Confinement, Elephant Grass or a Dreadnought on your big turn, then attack.
- **I cut another Mana Leak for 1 Arcane Denial.** On the combo turn you can cast it free under Dream Halls, and it's a hard counter, while Mana Leak can just be paid for later in the game. The 2 cards the opponent draws come on your extra turn. Arcane Denial is what the real Dream Halls lists play (80% run it).
- **Sideboard:** I swapped 2 Misdirection for 2 Chill to help against Sligh plus Goblins (14% of the field together). I also went from 2 Chain of Vapor to 1 because one moved to the main, and from 1 Annul to 2 (it counters Seal, Confinement and Phyrexian Dreadnought).

## Why the key cards
- **Show and Tell + Dream Halls:** the fastest way to turn on the engine.
- **Intuition:** naming three Dream Halls guarantees you get one, whatever your opponent picks.
- **Merchant Scroll:** fetches Intuition, Frantic Search, Opportunity or Chain of Vapor.
- **Opportunity:** under Dream Halls it costs 2 cards and draws 4, so you gain 2 cards each time.
- **Morphling:** has shroud on demand, which matters against Terrageddon's Swords to Plowshares (4 copies in 91.9% of lists).
- **Palinchron:** untaps your lands when it enters, which pays for Morphling's pumps.

## Mana (measured, 5,000 simulated games)
- **Mulligans:** 8.7%.
- **Mana screw:** 21.8%, versus 22.2% for the latest real Dream Halls list.
- **Blue when needed:** 97–99% of games by turn, versus 94–98% for the real list.
- **Average lands in play:** 3.22 by turn 4 and 3.71 by turn 5. Ancient Tomb and City of Traitors each count as two mana, so hard-casting Dream Halls on turn 4–5 is realistic.
- **Chance of seeing Dream Halls or Show and Tell by turn 4:** 79%. Counting Intuition and Merchant Scroll as ways to find them, it's 94.6%.
- **Chance of drawing both Dream Halls and Show and Tell naturally by turn 4:** only 26.5%. That's why the tutors matter.
- **Land count:** the checker suggests about 25.7 lands. That's a generic number based on average mana value. Real Dream Halls lists run 19.1, so 21 is a deliberate middle ground.

## Sideboarding
- **Sligh / Goblins (worst matchup):** bring in +2 Hydroblast, +2 Blue Elemental Blast, +2 Chill. Take out 2 Time Warp, 1 Arcane Denial, 1 Opportunity, and 2 Svyelunite Temple or 1–2 Ancient Tomb (Tomb's 2 damage per tap hurts here).
- **Stiflenought (bad):** bring in +2 Defense Grid, +1 Annul (for Dreadnought), +1 Stifle (it can counter Palinchron's untap trigger or Dreadnought's sacrifice trigger). Take out 2 Time Warp, 1 Mana Leak, 1 Chain of Vapor. Expect Hydroblast/BEB, Annul, Stifle and Daze from them. Try to force the issue through Defense Grid on your own turn.
- **Enchantress:** bring in +2 Annul, +1 Chain of Vapor. Take out 2 Mana Leak, 1 Time Warp. Save your bounce for Solitary Confinement or Elephant Grass during the turn you attack.
- **Terrageddon:** bring in +2 Teferi's Response (against Wasteland and Rishadan Port). Take out 1 Arcane Denial, 1 Chain of Vapor. Their Aura of Silence and Naturalize can hit Dream Halls, so cast it with protection up when you can.
- **Hermit Druid Combo:** bring in +1 Tormod's Crypt, +1 Stifle, +2 Defense Grid. Take out 2 Time Warp, 1 Opportunity, 1 Chain of Vapor.
- **Moneyball Black (discard):** bring in Defense Grid. Show and Tell plays around discard poorly, so lean on Intuition at instant speed.

## Label and what's unverified
- **Label:** brew. It borrows its mana (Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors, Svyelunite Temple, Saprazzan Skerry) and part of its sideboard from the real Dream Halls archetype. The win condition is new: Time Stretch and Time Warp show 0 recent lists in the results.
- **Damage math:** the roughly 18 damage from one Time Stretch with Morphling and Palinchron is my estimate, not a simulation. The simulator only plays land drops and mana, not the chain itself.
- **Matchups:** the matchup calls are my judgment from the opponents' decklists, not results from real games.
- **Dead cards:** without Dream Halls, the Time spells, Opportunity and Palinchron are close to uncastable. Expect some clunky hands.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
I made one change, all in the sideboard. The main deck I submitted is the same as stage 1's.

## The plan
This is Izzet Elementals built so each "when this enters" ability goes off two or three times. Peter Parker's Camera, Echo and Gogo copy those abilities, and Twinflame Travelers makes each one trigger an extra time. The abilities you're copying are the Incarnations' cheap evoke casts (Vibrance shoots 3 damage, Deceit bounces a permanent, Wistfulness draws two and discards one) and Champion of the Path. Champion deals damage equal to an entering Elemental's power to each opponent, and Twinflame and the Camera multiply that damage. Sunderflock finishes by returning every non-Elemental creature to its owner's hand.

## Why these cards
- **Camera (1 mana, 3 film counters, {2} and tap to copy any triggered or activated ability):** it's the cheapest copier and works on any ability. Echo ({1}) and Gogo ({X}{X}) back it up, but they only work once they've survived on the battlefield.
- **Twinflame Travelers:** it doubles every Elemental trigger for free, Champion's damage included. With the Camera on top, one evoked Vibrance can fire three times.
- **Eclipsed Flamekin:** it digs four cards deep for an Elemental or a land, so it finds pieces or land drops.
- **Burst Lightning, Prismari Charm and Get Out:** these are the interaction proven in Elementals lists. Burst and Charm each show up in about 97–99.5% of them. Charm's bounce mode also deals with artifacts.

## Mana (simulated over 5,000 games)
- **Lands:** 23, giving 21 blue sources and 18 red.
- **Mulligans:** 16.8%, compared with 8.5% for a recent top Elementals list.
- **Missing land drops:** 8.7% screw versus that list's 25%, and 2.6% flood.
- **Colors:** you have the right colors 97.3% of the time by turn 2 and 99.2% by turn 4.
- **Full combo:** a copier, an Incarnation and Champion are all in hand by turn 4 in 25.8% of games. That's the whole combo; one copier plus one trigger shows up much more often.

The deck checker says to cut about 3 lands, because real Elementals lists run 20.2. I tested 22 lands instead and it was worse: 19.3% mulligans and 10.5% screw. Those lists use Opt and Sleight of Hand to smooth their draws, and this deck doesn't, so I kept 23.

## Worst matchups and what changed
I looked up the top decks' lists. Two cards really threaten this engine:
- **Clarion Conqueror** shuts off activated abilities of artifacts and creatures, so the Camera, Echo and Gogo all stop working. It's in 90% of Boros Dragons lists, and Lifegain and Azorius Control also play it.
- **Torpor Orb** stops creatures' enter abilities from triggering, so there's nothing left to copy. It's in 73.6% of Landfall sideboards and 23.5% of Dimir Midrange sideboards, and some Landfall and Artifacts lists play it main deck.

The old sideboard couldn't remove an artifact. Colorstorm Stallion also does little here, since it needs instants and sorceries and this deck only has 8. So I made these swaps:
- **Out:** 3 Colorstorm Stallion, 1 Spell Pierce
- **In:** 2 Abrade (3 damage to a creature or destroy an artifact), 1 Annul, 1 Negate

**Sideboard guide (judgment):**
- **Jund Sacrifice (11.2% of the field):** bring in 2 Slagstorm and 2 Flashfreeze; take out 2 Wistfulness, Get Out and 1 Deceit. They bring in Duress, which can take the Camera, so get your copies going early.
- **Dimir Midrange (9.7%):** bring in Negate, Annul, 1 Abrade and Spell Pierce; take out 2 Burst Lightning, 1 Vibrance and Get Out.
- **Landfall (9.3%):** bring in 2 Flashfreeze, 2 Abrade and Annul; take out 2 Wistfulness, Get Out, Gogo and 1 Echo. Keep Sunderflock, since it bounces their creatures.
- **Boros Dragons (8.2%):** bring in 2 Abrade, 2 Broadside Barrage, 2 Flashfreeze and Disdainful Stroke; take out 2 Wistfulness, Gogo, 2 Camera and Get Out. Kill Clarion Conqueror before trying to copy anything. Their Voice of Victory means you can't cast spells during their turn, so play your interaction on your own turn.
- **Prowess (5.6%):** bring in Slagstorm and Broadside Barrage; take out Wistfulness and Gogo.
- **Lifegain (6.6%):** bring in Sunspine Lynx, which stops life gain. It also deals damage to you for each of your nonbasic lands, and this deck has 16.
- **Reanimator:** bring in 2 Ghost Vacuum.

The weakest main-deck slots are the single Gogo (legendary, and its {X}{X} cost is expensive) and the single Get Out. Stage 1 locked the engine, so I left them in.

## Label
This is a **brew**. The lands and interaction come from the Elementals deck, which is 9.5% of the field. The copy engine is new: the Camera has appeared in only 1 list in the last 90 days, and Twinflame Travelers, Echo, Champion of the Path and Eclipsed Flamekin in none.

## Not tested
- **Matchups:** how this does against each deck is my judgment, not tested. The simulator only checks land and color draws; it doesn't play out card abilities.
- **Combo math:** the copy counts are my reading of the rules text, not tested. For example, Twinflame plus a Camera activation should give three Vibrance shots.
- **Roaming Throne:** I didn't add it. It's another trigger doubler, played in the 3% of Elementals lists that use the Incarnations, and it's worth trying in place of Gogo.

Submitting.

I couldn't finish this build. **submit_deck rejected the deck, so it isn't registered.** The validator contradicts itself, and I tried all three ways to enter the list:
- With Atraxa only as commander, it says she must be in the main deck.
- With Atraxa as commander and also in the main deck, it says she's an illegal second copy.

# Mono-Red Magda Dwarves (Duel Commander), tuned

**Commander:** Magda, the Hoardmaster. Magda, Brazen Outlaw is in the 99. (See the note at the end about which Magda leads.)

## The plan
You curve cheap Dwarves and changelings into low-crew Vehicles and attack from turn 2. Brazen Outlaw gives your other Dwarves +1/+0 and makes a Treasure every time a Dwarf becomes tapped. Hoardmaster makes a tapped Treasure (once per turn) whenever you target the opponent or their stuff, so your burn spells feed her. Treasures speed you into your big threats. With five, Brazen Outlaw puts Embercleave, Sword of Fire and Ice, Jitte or a Dragon (Goldspan, Smaug) straight from your library onto the battlefield. With three, Hoardmaster makes a 4/4 flying, hasty Dragon token.

## Why the key cards
- **Magus of the Moon:** It turns every nonbasic land into a Mountain. That's strong against greedy multicolour mana like Slimefoot and Squee, Aragorn and Kraum/Yoshimaru, and against the Brigid deck's fetchlands and dual lands.
- **Hexing Squelcher:** Your spells can't be countered, and your creatures get "Ward — pay 2 life." This is your card against Jace, Nick Fury, Ral and Tasigur.
- **Fury, Pyrokinesis, Mizzium Mortars, Fiery Confluence:** Cheap ways to kill several small creatures at once. Brigid's mana creatures and Cloud's Mother of Runes and Giver of Runes are the targets.
- **Sword of Fire and Ice:** Protection from red and blue keeps the equipped creature safe from opposing red removal and blue bounce.

## What I changed (shell only; the engine is untouched)
- **Cut:** Axgard Artisan (it needs +1/+1 counters and the deck barely makes them), Shared Animosity (a 3-mana card that does nothing on its own), Light Up the Stage, Bombur, Gentle Dreamer (doesn't untap until you have three artifacts/legendaries/Sagas), and Glóin, Dwarf Emissary. I cut Glóin for mana reasons, without reviewing its text.
- **Added:** Springleaf Drum, Clown Car, Screaming Nemesis and Rubble Rouser. All four are in every one of the 9 recent Brazen Outlaw lists, and the Drum and Rouser give Dwarves extra ways to tap for Treasures. I also added a 30th Mountain.

## Mana (5,000 simulated games)
- 38 lands plus 3 spells that can be played as lands, all red.
- **Before the extra Mountain:** 19.6% mulligans and 65.3% of games hit every land drop through turn 4. The real Brazen Outlaw list does 17.3% and 70%.
- **After:** 18.6% mulligans, 67.3% on land drops. Red mana is fine on 98.9–99.9% of turns. The deck still stumbles a little more than the proven list, so mulligan one-landers.
- **Draw odds (exact):** 62.5% to have a 1–2 mana Dwarf or changeling by turn 2 on the play. 59.2% to have one of your 9 cheap removal spells by turn 3.

## Matchups and adjustments
I didn't submit a sideboard. These are play patterns and swaps for your next event.
- **Cloud, Midgar Mercenary (11.3% of the field, the biggest deck):** Probably your worst matchup. It's a white equipment deck with Mother and Giver of Runes, Parallax Wave, Swords to Plowshares, Solitude, Jitte and its own Sword of Fire and Ice. Its Sword gives protection from red, which blanks your burn and blocks your red attackers. Kill Mother and Giver right away, and save Abrade, Embereth Shieldbreaker and Plundering Barbarian for its equipment. Magus of the Moon does little here: Cloud plays about 26 snow Plains.
- **Brigid, Clachan's Heart (7%):** A green-white deck full of mana creatures, with Earthcraft and Devoted Druid. Fury, Pyrokinesis and Mortars are your best cards here. Magus also hits its fetchlands and duals.
- **Blue decks (Jace, Winter, Nick Fury, Ral, Tasigur):** Squelcher and Pyroblast come first. Deal damage early and use Fireblast to finish.
- **Slimefoot and Squee, Aragorn, Kraum:** Get Magus down on turn 3.
- **Possible swaps:** Winter Moon or Tangle Wire from the proven list are worth testing against the multicolour decks. Winter Moon is weak against Cloud.

## Label and unverified points
- This is **tuned** from the recent Magda, Brazen Outlaw lists (9 lists).
- **Commander choice:** The plan you approved has Brazen Outlaw as commander, but the deck checker only accepted the list with Brazen Outlaw in the 99, so Hoardmaster is the commander. Both are mono-red 2-drop Dwarves and legal either way. The 9 recent Brazen Outlaw lists lead with Brazen Outlaw and keep Hoardmaster in the 99. I'd suggest swapping them; that version passed the deck checker as legal.
- **Not verified:** I didn't look up the rules text of every original shell card (Thorin, Dáin, Óin, Gimli and others). Matchup calls are judgment, not results. No tool tested actual games against these decks.

# Esper Cephalid Breakfast (Premodern brew)

## The plan
You play Cephalid Illusionist, then Nomads en-Kor or Shaman en-Kor. The en-Kor has a free {0} ability that targets Illusionist, and every time Illusionist is targeted you mill three cards. Repeat that until your whole library is in the graveyard. Then Animate Dead, Exhume or Necromancy brings back Sutured Ghoul. As it enters, it exiles every creature you milled (four 5/3 Twisted Abominations, a 6/6 Scion of Darkness, the en-Kors) and becomes a huge trampler. Dragon Breath then comes back from the graveyard onto the Ghoul, because the Ghoul has mana value 7, and gives it haste so you attack the same turn. Lethal is usually around 30 or more trample damage. That number is my rough sum of the creature cards, not a measurement.

## Why these cards
- **Illusionist + en-Kor:** Two cheap creatures that mill your whole library for no mana. Nobody in this field plays against this combo.
- **Intuition (3):** A second way to find Illusionist.
- **Twisted Abomination:** It adds power to the Ghoul, and when it's in your hand early, Swampcycling {2} finds a Swamp.
- **Eight ways to reanimate:** Exhume dodges Seal of Cleansing, because Exhume isn't an aura. Necromancy can be cast at instant speed. If the opponent stops the Ghoul, you can reanimate an Abomination or Scion as backup.
- **Cabal Therapy, Duress, Lim-Dûl's Vault:** Discard to clear the way and a card to dig for missing pieces. Cabal Therapy's flashback lets you sacrifice a spare en-Kor.

## Mana (5,000 simulated games)
The deck has 23 lands. That's one more than the 22 the build stage reported, and the deck checker confirmed it. Sources: 18 black, 15 blue, 15 white.
- **Mulligans and land problems:** 16.8% mulligan rate, 8.7% screw, 2.6% flood. The top Hermit Druid list measured 19.7%, 10.4% and 1.9%.
- **Colors:** You have the right colors 80% of the time on turn 1 and 92.9% by turn 4. Hermit Druid measured 86.1% and 97.6%. City of Brass and Gemstone Mine cost you a bit early.
- **The real weakness:** All three pieces (Illusionist or Intuition, an en-Kor, and a reanimation spell) are in hand and castable by turn 4 only **30.6%** of the time. That number doesn't count digging with Lim-Dûl's Vault or cycling Abominations, so the real rate is somewhat higher. It's still a deck that wins through card selection and patience, not a reliable turn-3 kill.

## Worst matchups (my review against the current field)
- **Enchantress (12.5% of the field, most played): harder than the build stage claimed.**
  - Elephant Grass is main deck in 52.6% of lists and says black creatures can't attack you. Every creature you'd win with is black.
  - Solitary Confinement (99.6%) prevents all damage to its controller. It also gives them shroud, so Duress and Cabal Therapy can't target them anymore.
  - They also run Seal of Cleansing (100%), which kills Animate Dead or Necromancy, and Tormod's Crypt in 97.8% of sideboards.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** Swords to Plowshares on your Ghoul gains them about 30 life. They also run four Wasteland against your 18 nonbasic lands, plus Armageddon.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%):** Stifle can counter any of your key triggers. Powder Keg on 1 kills Nomads en-Kor, and on 2 it kills Illusionist and Shaman en-Kor. Back to Basics is in 65% of sideboards and hits your 18 nonbasic lands hard.
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins:** Bolts, Grim Lavamancer and Mogg Fanatic kill the 1-toughness combo creatures, and your painlands speed up their clock.

## What I changed (sideboard only, engine untouched)
- **Out:** 2 Circle of Protection: Red, 1 Engineered Plague. CoP: Red protects your life total but not your combo creatures.
- **In:** 2 Disenchant (now 3), 1 Meddling Mage (now 3). Disenchant answers Elephant Grass, Solitary Confinement, Back to Basics, Tormod's Crypt and Sligh's enchantments and artifacts.

## Sideboarding guide
- **Enchantress:** +3 Disenchant, +1 Duress, +2 or 3 Meddling Mage (name Solitary Confinement or Seal of Cleansing). Take out Lim-Dûl's Vault and Necromancy. Cast discard before Confinement lands, because shroud blanks it afterward.
- **Terrageddon:** +3 Meddling Mage (name Swords or Armageddon), +1 Duress, +1 or 2 Disenchant for Crypt. Take out Vault and one Exhume, since Exhume can hand them a Terravore. Fetch basics with Abominations whenever you can.
- **Stiflenought:** +3 Meddling Mage (name Stifle first), +1 Duress, +2 Swords for Dreadnought, +1 or 2 Disenchant for Back to Basics and Powder Keg. Take out Exhume and some Abominations.
- **Sligh:** +3 Hydroblast, +2 Exalted Angel. Take out Duress and Vault. Mind your life total with the painlands.
- **Goblins:** +1 Engineered Plague (name Goblin), +3 Hydroblast.

## Label
This is a **brew**. The graveyard-kill package (Sutured Ghoul, Dragon Breath, Animate Dead and Exhume, Cabal Therapy) and the 3-color mana come from Hermit Druid Combo. The Cephalid Breakfast engine has very little results data: Illusionist shows 2 lists in the last 90 days and Shaman en-Kor shows 1.

## Not verified
- **Win rates:** No tool measured any matchup. The matchup notes above are my judgment, based on what's in opposing lists.
- **Deck size:** I haven't confirmed that a typical game leaves enough creature power in the graveyard. It depends on how many creatures you've already drawn.
- **Decking:** Milling your whole library and then failing means you lose to decking. You can stop activating the en-Kor at any point, so mill only as deep as you need.
